video_title: Coach Daigneault on OKC's Compete Level | Postgame Media | November 23, 2026

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on OKC's defensive shortcomings and thin margins
quotes.excerpt: defensively we left something to be desired tonight. Obviously our margins are a little thin with our size
quotes.quote: I thought obviously offensively we were pretty good tonight. 120 points is enough to win anywhere, home or road. Defensively we left something to be desired tonight. Obviously our margins are a little thin with our size, but that's a gift. If you want to get better, it really puts the spotlight on the need to be really tight on multiple possessions and they put a lot of pressure on you offensively obviously with the pace and the pace in the halfcourt. So we were behind a lot of plays where we could have been better, but I thought we really competed.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on the Thunder defensive struggles despite scoring 120 points. He notes that while the team is competing hard, their thin margins due to size require them to be much tighter on every possession.

structured.context: Head coach Mark Daigneault discusses the team's defensive performance and offensive output following a loss.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on the challenges of playing small ball
quotes.excerpt: we're playing small and the margins on that are thinner, especially when you're going against size
quotes.quote: We're playing small and the margins on that are thinner, especially when you're going against size. I thought that showed up last night and tonight. So some of it is structural despite the effort, but it just puts that much more of an emphasis on the need to execute. And like I said, it's a gift. These games are tough. We're giving ourselves a chance in some of these closer games where a couple plays away and that puts the spotlight on every single detail, every single possession and that's an opportunity for us to look in the mirror and improve because obviously it stings when you lose.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault says playing small ball creates thinner margins for the Thunder. He views the current challenges as a gift that forces the team to focus on every single detail and possession to improve.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault explains the structural challenges of playing small ball against larger opponents.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on the impact of Kenrich Williams
quotes.excerpt: he does it on both ends, does it on the glass, good offensive rebounder, good defensive rebounder
quotes.quote: He does it on both ends, does it on the glass, good offensive rebounder, good defensive rebounder. He's guarding Zubac at times tonight, he's guarding Siakam obviously at times tonight. And then offensively, to your point, great system skills, good spacer, good screener, plays on the catch quickly, makes good decisions. So he had a great game, gave us a great effort tonight. I thought P.V. similar, I thought he gave us great minutes tonight. I thought Siakam, for as good as he is and as much as they play through him, right now with Haliburton out, he had the couple catch and shoot threes that hurt us, but his ISO game that's usually very reliable for them, I thought we really made him earn everything.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault praises Kenrich Williams for his versatility and system skills after a strong effort against the Pacers. He also highlights the team defensive effort in making Pascal Siakam earn his points.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault evaluates the performance of Kenrich Williams and discusses the impact of opposing players during the game.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on the team's consistent competitive effort
quotes.excerpt: I don't think any of these games have really been a lack of effort
quotes.quote: I don't think any of these games have really been a lack of effort. I don't think it's like we're not showing up or not wanting to win or laying it on the line. Guys are gutting it out and putting their best foot forward from a competitive standpoint and we never take that for granted. Win or lose, we want to be a team that competes together every night and I think we're doing that. We just have some guys out and we're having to scramble on that and it's putting a huge emphasis on our ability to execute. We're probably three or four plays away tonight from being able to come out of here with a win.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault defends the team effort level despite recent losses. He says the team is gutting it out and competing every night, but they are currently just a few plays away from winning games while dealing with injuries.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault addresses the team's competitive effort and the impact of missing players on execution.
